The provided table is a “Contents” index page from the **DBMERG Manual, Service Pack 2025-4 Build 146** (SOFiSTiK AG). It functions as a navigational map for the manual section titled **“Task Description”** and its subsequent **“Input Description”** chapter. The table is formatted as a two-column listing where the **left side contains section/subsection titles** and the **right side contains page numbers** (e.g., “1-1”, “2-1”, “2-2”, etc.). The visible portion includes the main heading, the start of the Input Description chapter, and a structured list of subsections with their corresponding pages.

### Structure and meaning
- **Header area**
  - “Task Description” (page **1-1**) appears at the top, indicating the chapter/section where the program purpose is described.
- **Section: Input Description**
  - “Input Description” (page **2-1**) is the main next entry. It introduces how the program input is organized.
- **Subsections under Input Description**
  Each subsection is listed with its title and page number:
  - **2.1 Input Language** → page **2-1**
  - **2.2 Input Records** → page **2-1**
  - **2.3 CDB – Selection of a database** → page **2-2**
  - **2.4 CTRL – Control options** → page **2-3**
    - **2.4.1 REST Restart-Steuerung** → page **2-3**
  - **2.5 LC – Load Cases** → page **2-4**
  - **2.6 GRP – Group Assignment** → page **2-5**
  - **2.7 NODE – Nodal Values** → page **2-7**
  - **2.8 BEMA – Beam Elements** → page **2-8**

  - **2.14 EXTR – Data mapping 2D-3D** → page **2-14**
  - **2.15 ECHO – Volume of Output** → page **2-15**
- **Example entry**
  - “Example” appears at the end, page **3-1**, indicating the next chapter after the input description.

### Context for RAG use
This index ties directly to how **DBMERG** transfers/merges data between SOFiSTiK databases: it points to the mechanisms used to select source/target databases (**CDB**), define control behavior (**CTRL/REST**), specify load cases and mapping rules (**LC**, **GRP**), and define which result quantities to copy for different element and node types (**NODE**, **BEMA**, **TRUS**, **CABL**, **SPRI**, **QUAD**, **BRIC**) including specialized mapping between 2D and 3D (**EXTR**) and output verbosity (**ECHO**). The “Example” section suggests there is a worked use-case later in the manual.

 1 Task Description
 Program DBMERG allows the modification or transfer of data within a data base or between data bases of the SOFiSTiK-Software. The program may be used for merging results from different tasks, the treatment of multiple used parts or the transfer of primary load states.
 The program has functions as follows:
 Import of loads or results
 - Distribution or results or properties of elements

Program DBMERG allows the modification or transfer of data within a data base or between data bases of the SOFiSTiK-Software. The program may be used for merging results from different tasks, the treatment of multiple used parts or the transfer of primary load states.. The program has functions as follows:. Import of loads or results. - Distribution or results or properties of elements.
 - Changing results with factors
 These functions require a special responsability of the user, because the check of those results may become extremely difficult.
 DBMERG uses one or two SOFiSTiK-databases, each of them needs a static system. When calling the program a second data base will be opened with the name of the input file. This will be the source, while the project data base is the target.
 Elements and nodes of the project data base will be assigned to those in the source data base via groups and load cases. Grouping within DBMERG extends beyond the general SOFiSTiK group mechanisms.
 DBMERG will copy all results from the source to the target and will replace load cases and or element or node numbers.
The input occurs in a free format with the CADINP input language (see the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’FEA / STRUCTURAL Installation and Basics’).

This table is a record-to-items specification for a SOFiSTiK-style input data format. It is organized into **blocks**, where each block concludes with the record **END**. An **empty block** indicated by **END/END** terminates the program. Within each block, **at most one external database** may be used. The table also references that the standard records **HEAD**, **END**, and **PAGE** follow the general manual “FEA / STRUCTURAL Installation and Basics”.

The main content of the table lists record keywords and their associated **parameters** (items). Conceptually, each record defines a set of identifiers or properties, often by mapping one range/order of values to another using “FROM / TO / INC” patterns.

### Records and their items

- **CDB**
  - Items: **FROM**, **PASS**
  - Purpose (inferred from naming/structure): selects a database or dataset reference using a starting index (**FROM**) and a pass/version/control value (**PASS**).

- **MAT**
  - Items: **FROM**, **TO**, **INC**, **BY**
  - Purpose: defines a mapping or enumeration of **material** identifiers. Values can be generated from **FROM** to **TO** with step **INC**, and the progression/selection can be further parameterized by **BY**.

- **SECT**
  - Items: **FROM**, **TO**, **INC**, **BY**
  - Purpose: similar to MAT, but for **cross-sectional** properties (sections). Allows bulk assignment/selection across a range.

- **LC**
  - Items: **NO**, **NOS**
  - Purpose: selects/defines load cases or similar numbered entities. **NO** denotes a single number or starting case; **NOS** likely specifies a second or count/range endpoint used to define multiple cases.

- **GRP**
  - Items: **NO**, **NOS**
  - Purpose: selects/defines a **group** (e.g., loading group, parameter group) with numbering similar to **LC**.

### Entity definition records (degrees of freedom / components)

These records declare **node- or element-type** variables by listing a **TYPE** and multiple component values.

- **NODE**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FX**, **FY**, **FZ**, **FXX**, **FYY**, **FZZ**
  - Purpose: defines nodal load/support-like constraints or actions in translational directions (**FX/FY/FZ**) and additional symmetric/second-order components (**FXX/FYY/FZZ**), all governed by a **TYPE** selector.

- **BEAM**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FN**, **FVY**, **FVZ**, **FMT**, **FMY**, **FMZ**, **FMB**
  - Purpose: defines beam-related components (forces/moments). **FN** typically represents an axial component; **FVY/FVZ** transverse/shear components; **FMT** and **FMY/FMZ** moment components; **FMB** an additional moment/branch component. All controlled by **TYPE**.

- **TRUS**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FN**
  - Purpose: truss member action defined mainly by **FN** (axial force), with behavior controlled by **TYPE**.

- **CABL**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FN**
  - Purpose: cable member action defined primarily by **FN**, governed by **TYPE**.

- **SPRI**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FN**
  - Purpose: spring action; **FN** is the main force parameter (e.g., spring force), with **TYPE** selecting spring behavior/direction/type.

- **QUAD**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FMX**, **FMY**, **FMXY**, **FVX**, **FVY**, **FNX**, **FNY**, **FNXY**
  - Purpose: quadrilateral surface/member action with a rich set of membrane and shear components. **FMX/FMY** and **FMXY** resemble membrane force resultants; **FVX/FVY** shear-like components; **FNX/FNY/FNXY** normal-related components. Selection is controlled by **TYPE**.

- **BRIC**
  - Items: **TYPE**, **FSX**, **FSY**, **FSZ**, **FTAU**
  - Purpose: brick/solid element action with directional components (**FSX/FSY/FSZ**) and a shear/torsion-type quantity (**FTAU**). Controlled by **TYPE**.

- **ECHO**
  - Items: **OPT**, **VAL**
  - Purpose: controls output echoing/verbosity. **OPT** selects the echo option; **VAL** provides the value or setting.

Overall, this table provides a compact schema for bulk parameterization (MAT/SECT/LC/GRP ranges) and for defining element/node load components via **TYPE**-dependent sets of forces and moments (NODE/BEAM/TRUS/CABL/SPRI/QUAD/BRIC), with program control and documentation handled by **CDB** and **ECHO**, and standard block termination by **END**.

The following records are defined:
 Input is organized in blocks. Every block ends with the record END. An empty block (END/END) will terminate the program. Within every Block a single external database may be used.
 The records HEAD, END and PAGE are described in the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’FEA / STRUCTURAL Installation and Basics’.

The table describes the parameters for a command section related to selecting a database source used “for the merging” (as indicated by the contextual note). It specifies what input fields can be provided in the command block and how they map to database selection and access.

**Overall purpose**  
This input block allows the user to define which database file should be used as the *source* for any import/merge operation. The context text clarifies additional behavior: if the record name is provided only, the *master project* will be used again as the source. It also notes a structural constraint: “A definition is only possible once in every input block,” meaning each parameter definition should be stated a single time per block to avoid duplication/conflict.

**Columns**  
- **Item**: The parameter/field name used in the command.  
- **Description**: What the parameter means and how it functions.  
- **Unit**: The expected data type/format annotation used by the system (e.g., “Lit256”, “Lit16”). These are likely fixed literal/string length classes rather than physical units.  
- **Default**: The default value when the parameter is not explicitly set.

**Rows / parameters**  
1. **FROM**  
   - **Description**: “File name of a database.” This is the primary selector for the merge/import source. By specifying the database filename here, the command knows which external database should be used as input.  
   - **Unit**: `Lit256` (treated as a literal/string value up to a certain size constraint).  
   - **Default**: `!` (a placeholder indicating it is required or that no meaningful default exists; in many command syntaxes, `!` is used to denote mandatory input).

2. **PASS**  
   - **Description**: “Optional password for protected database.” This field is used only if the database referenced by `FROM` is access-protected. If the database is not password-protected, this parameter can be omitted.  
   - **Unit**: `Lit16`.  
   - **Default**: `-` (indicating no password is provided by default, or that the field is optional and effectively empty).

**Implications for use in a merge workflow**  
When performing a merge/import, the system expects at least a valid database filename in `FROM`. If that database requires authentication, `PASS` should be supplied. Additionally, definitions must be provided once per input block, so repeated `FROM`/`PASS` definitions within the same block are not allowed.

CDB
 For the merging this command selects a database to be used as source for any import. If the record name is given only, the master project will be used again. A definition is only possible once in every input block.

The table describes a single configuration field used in a software/control context. It has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The only row shown corresponds to the parameter named **OPT**.

### Item: OPT
- **Meaning / Purpose:** **OPT** is a selector for choosing among multiple operational modes or behaviors. The description states: “One of the following options: …”, indicating that **OPT** must be set to one of a predefined set of string values.
- **Allowed option(s):** The table lists **REST** as an available option, described as **“restart control.”**  
  - This suggests that setting `OPT` to `REST` enables or configures *restart-related control logic* in the system.
- **Interpretation:** The name and phrasing imply that **OPT** does not take a numeric value; instead, it selects a control strategy or feature mode. In a configuration or command specification, `OPT=REST` would likely govern how restart behavior is handled (e.g., when and how the system restarts, or what control mechanism is used during restart).

### Unit
- The **Unit** column for this parameter shows **`LIT`**. This appears to be a textual/unit tag rather than a physical unit (e.g., not seconds or meters). In many configuration schemas, a unit field may represent an expected datatype or category token. Here, `LIT` likely indicates a **literal/string** value.

### Default
- The **Default** column contains **“-”**, indicating there is **no predefined default value** provided in the table. Therefore, **OPT** may be **required** to be explicitly set by the user/system integrator, or it may rely on upstream defaults not shown in this excerpt.

### Overall structure and usage implication
This excerpt is a small slice of a larger configuration documentation table. It specifies that **OPT** is an enumerated parameter with at least one documented value (**REST**), and that it is associated with a literal/string-style input (`LIT`) and has no explicit default. For RAG purposes, the key facts to store are: **OPT selects an operational option; REST corresponds to restart control; expected value type is literal/string; default is unspecified.**
CTRL

By defualt, possibly existing results of the target load case are deleted pior to copying.
 The restart option CTRL REST 1 suppresses deletion of load case dependent data (results) for the target load case. This allows, e.g., to realize different mapping rules (GRP ...) for nodal results and elemental results in subsequent DBMERG runs.

The table defines two input fields used to control load case selection and remapping when performing a DBMERG operation. The purpose of these fields is to specify how results are transferred from an “old” load case to a “new” load case, either within the same model database or across databases, depending on the configuration.

**Columns**
- **Item**: Short field identifier.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of the field.
- **Unit**: Indicates that the fields are identifiers rather than measured quantities (shown as “–”).
- **Default**: Default behavior/value if the user does not provide an override.

**Fields**
1. **NO (New load case number)**
   - **Description**: Specifies the target load case number that results will be written to as part of DBMERG.
   - **Unit**: “–” (not a physical unit; it is an integer/identifier).
   - **Default**: “*”.
   - **Interpretation of default**: The asterisk indicates that there is no fixed literal default number; instead, NO typically operates as a required or dynamically determined destination load case number. In other words, the software expects a meaningful new load case identifier (either provided by the user or generated/selected according to the DBMERG workflow).

2. **NOS (Old load case number)**
   - **Description**: Specifies the source (existing) load case number from which results are copied/merged.
   - **Unit**: “–”.
   - **Default**: **NO**.
   - **Meaning of default**: If NOS is left unchanged, the operation uses the same load case number for both source and destination—i.e., it effectively maps old load case = new load case.

**Contextual behavior (from provided text)**
- “Any action of DBMERG will use the selected load cases only.” This table therefore supports explicitly controlling which load cases participate in the merge/copy operation.
- With the input of **NOS**, results can be copied to *other* load case numbers (source differs from target).
- In combination with element grouping, different blocks can assign results for different elements of the same load case to different load cases of the same element. This enables fine-grained remapping rather than a single global load case transfer.
- The text notes that the default **NO = NOS** mapping (i.e., same load case number for both old and new) is only possible under a condition where **two data bases are open**. Practically, this means the software may require both source and destination contexts to align when relying on the implicit mapping behavior.

Overall, the table encodes a load-case remapping rule: **NO** selects the destination load case, while **NOS** optionally selects a different source load case; if NOS defaults to NO, the mapping is identity unless the application context dictates otherwise.

LC
 Any action of DBMERG will use the selected load cases only. With input of NOS you may copy results to other load case numbers.
 In combination with the grouping of the elements you may assign in different blocks results of different elments of the same load case to different load cases of the same element. The default NO=NOS is only posssible, if you have two data bases open.

This table documents the parameters used for the **GRP assignment mechanism** in the `DBMERG` data transfer process. It lists three items—**NO**, **NOS**, and **NDIV**—that together define how **elements (and optionally beams) in the source database** map to corresponding **elements in the target database**.

### Fields and meanings

1. **NO (Group number source data)**
   - **Purpose:** Specifies the **group number** that will be used to select elements in the **source data** (the database being merged from).
   - **Type/Unit:** No explicit unit (“–”); it is a logical grouping key.
   - **Default:** marked as **required** (`!`), meaning the value must be provided for GRP-based assignment to work correctly.

2. **NOS (Group number target data)**
   - **Purpose:** Specifies the **group number** in the **target data** (the base project database receiving data).
   - **Type/Unit:** No unit (“–”), also used as a logical grouping key.
   - **Default:** **`NO`**. In other words, if `NOS` is omitted, the mapping assumes **source group and target group are identical** (effectively a direct 1:1 correspondence under the GRP rules).

3. **NDIV (Group divisor)**
   - **Purpose:** Defines how the element/node numbers are converted into **group numbers**. The group number is computed as:
     - **group = floor(element_or_node_number / NDIV)** (described conceptually in the context as “division of the node or element number by NDIV”).
   - **Type/Unit:** No unit (“–”), purely a divisor for grouping arithmetic.
   - **Default:** `*` (asterisk), meaning it uses a system-defined/automatic behavior; typically it indicates that NDIV is not overridden unless explicitly set in the command.

### How these parameters function in DBMERG (contextual behavior)

Using these parameters, `DBMERG` assigns a source element to a target element when:
- their computed **group numbers match** according to **NDIV**, and
- their **modulus** condition (same remainder from division) also matches as stated in the context (elements are paired when both “modulus will be the same and the group numbers follow the specified assignment”).

Important nuances described alongside the GRP logic:
- **1:1 assignment** applies when no GRP-based input is given.
- **DBMERG can define groupings different from the database**, enabling specialized mapping.
- **Beam elements** require not only matching group/remainder rules, but also **identical beam length** to be assigned.
- If node numbering rules differ from element numbering rules, the user must separate blocks with different assignment definitions.

Finally, the process uses the **first valid assignment** found during evaluation. This enables a “default” mapping (placed last) that applies broadly, while more specific mappings (placed earlier) override it.

GRP
 For the transfer of data elements of the project base will be assigned to elements of the source database. Without any input a 1 to 1 assignement is in effect.
 The group number is given as division of the node or elementnumber by NDIV. Two elements will be assigned to each other if the modulus will be the same and the group numbers follow the specified assignment. In DBMERG you may define completely other groups than those which are defined in the database.
 Beam elements, however, will be assigned to each other only if the beam length is also identi- cal.
 If the node numbers do not follow the same rules as the elements, you have to use to seperate blocks with different assignements.
 This feature can be used to multiply the properties of prefabricated parts.
 Example:
 In the project data base are the elements 1001, 1002, 1003 as well as 1101, 1102, 1103 and 2001, 2002, 2003 defined. In the additional data base are the Elements 101, 102, 103 defined. Input of
 +PROG DBMERG HEAD GRP NO 9999 NOS 0 END
 defines the assignments:
 1101 := 101 , 1102 := 102 and 1103 := 103
 Elements 1001 to 1003 resp. 2001 to 2003 are without assignment. The results of elments 101 to 103 will be assigned to the elements 1101 to 1103.
 Input of:
 +PROG DBMERG HEAD GRP NO 10 NOS 1 NDIV 100 GRP NO 11 NOS 1 NDIV 100 END
 defines the assignments:
 1001 < = 101 , 1002 < = 102 und 1003 < = 103
 1101 < = 101 , 1102 < = 102 und 1103 < = 103

+PROG DBMERG HEAD GRP NO 10 NOS 1 NDIV 100 GRP NO 11 NOS 1 NDIV 100 END. defines the assignments:. 1001 < = 101 , 1002 < = 102 und 1003 < = 103. 1101 < = 101 , 1102 < = 102 und 1103 < = 103.
 and will thus copy the results multiple to the elements. And finally
 +PROG DBMERG HEAD GRP NO 9999 NOS 1 NDIV 100 END
 will assign:
 1001 < = 101 , 1002 < = 102 und 1003 < = 103
 1101 < = 101 , 1102 < = 102 und 1103 < = 103
 2001 < = 101 , 2002 < = 102 und 2003 < = 103
 For the data transfer the first valid assignment is used, multiple assignements are not checked, which allows to define a general default as last assignment, while more specific ones are defined first.

The table documents configuration options for selecting which analysis result data should be copied for a set of load cases and load groups (“For the selected load cases and groups the results will be copied.”). It is organized into four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

**Column meanings**
- **Item**: A short parameter name used in the interface/configuration.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of the parameter and the valid options (for the TYPE row) or the calculation role (for factor rows).
- **Unit**: The measurement/unit designation, when applicable. In this table, the **TYPE** row has unit **LIT** and factor entries use **—** (dimensionless).
- **Default**: The default value used when no explicit setting is provided.

**Row: TYPE**
- **Item**: `TYPE`
- **Purpose**: Chooses the **type of results** to operate on/copy.
- **Unit**: `LIT`
- **Default**: `ALL`
- **Allowed values (with meanings)**:
  - `NONE`: deactivates all values.
  - `ALL`: selects all values.
  - `LINK`: forces associated with kinematic constraints.
  - `LOAD`: nodal loads.
  - `DISP`: nodal displacements.
  - `REAC`: support reactions.
  - `VELO`: nodal velocities.
  - `ACCE`: nodal accelerations.
  - `MPHY`: multiphysics results.

This row effectively determines the category of result fields that subsequent scaling factors (if used) would apply to, depending on the system’s interpretation.

**Factor scaling rows (dimensionless)**
These rows define multiplicative **scaling factors** for different result components along axes and for rotations:
- **`FX`**: “Factor for displacements/forces in X”  
  - **Unit**: `—` (dimensionless)  
  - **Default**: `1.0`
- **`FY`**: “Factor for displacements/forces in Y”  
  - **Default**: `FX`
- **`FZ`**: “Factor for displacements/forces in Z”  
  - **Default**: `FY`

- **`FXX`**: “Factor for rotations/moments in X”  
  - **Default**: `FZ`
- **`FYY`**: “Factor for rotations/moments in Y”  
  - **Default**: `FXX`
- **`FZZ`**: “Factor for rotations/moments in Z”  
  - **Default**: `FYY`

**Implication of defaults**
The defaults form a cascading assignment chain: `FX` defaults to **1.0**, then `FY` inherits `FX`, `FZ` inherits `FY`, `FXX` inherits `FZ`, etc. This ensures all components share a consistent scale unless overridden individually.

Overall, the table specifies **(1)** which result types to include via **TYPE**, and **(2)** how to scale result components in translational (X/Y/Z) and rotational/moment (X/Y/Z) directions through **FX–FZZ**, using dimensionless factors.

NODE
 For the selected load cases and groups the results will be copied.

The table defines configuration inputs for a “BEAM” results workflow, specifically controlling which types of beam result quantities are processed and what scale factors apply to different force/moment components before copying results for the selected load cases and groups.

It has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each row specifies a parameter name (“Item”), explains its meaning (“Description”), indicates the expected unit or whether it is unitless, and gives a default value.

### Row group 1: Result type selection (Item: **TYPE**)
- **TYPE**: “Type of results to work on.”
- The **Default** is **LIT** (short for a selected set of result categories).
- The **Description** lists possible modes:
  - **NONE**: deactivates all values (no results processed).
  - **ALL**: selects all values.
  - **LOAD**: loading results.
  - **FORC**: internal forces and moments.
  - **STIF**: stiffnesses.
  - **EIGE**: secondary forces and moments.
  - **STRE**: stresses.
  - **REIN**: reinforcement.
  - **TEND**: tendons.
This parameter effectively filters the result categories that will be copied for the chosen load cases/groups.

### Row group 2: Scaling factors for beam force/moment components
All these parameters are scale factors applied to the corresponding result components. Their **Unit** column shows **“—”**, indicating they are unitless coefficients. The table provides both the parameter meaning and defaults:

- **FN**: “Factor for normal forces”  
  - **Default:** 1.0
- **FVY**: “Factor for shear forces in y”  
  - **Default:** FN (i.e., inherits the value of **FN**)
- **FVZ**: “Factor for shear forces in z”  
  - **Default:** FVY
- **FMT**: “Factor for torsional moments”  
  - **Default:** FVZ
- **FMY**: “Factor for bending moments in y”  
  - **Default:** FMT
- **FMZ**: “Factor for bending moments in z”  
  - **Default:** FMY
- **FMB**: “Factor for warping moments”  
  - **Default:** FMZ

### Interpretation of defaults (dependency chain)
The defaults establish a cascading relationship: **FVY defaults to FN**, **FVZ defaults to FVY**, then **FMT to FVZ**, continuing through **FMY**, **FMZ**, and **FMB**. As a result, if the user changes **FN**, all other related factors inherit that change unless explicitly overridden. This makes the scaling behavior consistent across different force and moment result components.

Overall, the table specifies: (1) what kinds of beam results are selected (**TYPE**), and (2) how those results are scaled component-by-component prior to being copied for specified load cases and groups.

BEAM
 For the selected load cases and groups the results will be copied.

The table defines configurable input fields for a structural/results processing workflow (context suggests a TRUS—likely a truss or structural analysis module). It contains two primary columns: **Item** (parameter name) and **Description** (what the parameter controls), plus **Unit** and **Default** values.

### 1) Item: **TYPE** (Result selection mode)
- **Purpose:** Specifies **what type of results** the system should work on.
- **Unit:** **LTT** (as listed in the table; no further dimensional meaning is provided in the excerpt, but it indicates the expected input category/unit for this field).
- **Default:** **ALL**

**Allowed options and meanings:**
- **NONE**: “deactivated all values” — disables all result categories (no processing of any result type).
- **ALL**: “selected all values” — enables processing for every result category supported by the system.
- **LOAD**: “Loading” — focuses on results associated with applied loads.
- **FORC**: “Internal forces and moments” — targets internal force/moment outputs (e.g., axial forces, bending moments, shear forces).
- **STRE**: “Design stresses” — targets stress results used for design/checking (e.g., computed stresses for design evaluation).

This parameter acts like a filter or switchboard determining which subsets of analysis outputs are included.

### 2) Item: **FN** (Factor for normal forces)
- **Purpose:** Provides a **scaling factor** applied specifically to **normal forces**.
- **Unit:** **—** (unitless, as indicated by a dash).
- **Default:** **1.0**

**Interpretation:**  
- A default of **1.0** means normal forces are used as-is.
- If changed, it would proportionally amplify or reduce the contribution of normal forces in whichever computations consume this factor.

Overall, the table establishes two key controls: **TYPE**, which selects which result domains are active (none/load/internal forces/design stresses), and **FN**, a numeric multiplier for normal-force-related calculations.
TRUS

The provided table fragment appears to be a configuration/parameter reference for a structural or loading-related computational workflow. It contains four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The table defines at least two parameters: **TYPE** and **FN**.

### Row: TYPE
- **Item:** `TYPE`
- **Description:** “Type of results to work on”
- **Selectable options (as listed in the Description cell):**
  - `NONE` — **deactivated all values**
  - `ALL` — **selected all values**
